nary_nodes.label: Ebola treatments trial begins
evidence: A trial of potential treatments for the species of virus behind the current deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has begun, the World Health Organization (WHO) has announced.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event marking the beginning of a trial, such as a medical or legal trial.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No existing candidate accurately represents the beginning of a trial, so a new event type is minted.

nary_nodes.label: WHO announced trial began
evidence: A trial of potential treatments for the species of virus behind the current deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has begun, the World Health Organization (WHO) has announced.

nary_nodes.label: First patient enrolled
evidence: The first patient has been enrolled in DR Congo, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Thursday.

nary_nodes.label: Confirmed Ebola cases
evidence: More than 1,400 cases and 438 deaths have been confirmed in the country, according to the WHO.

nary_nodes.label: Confirmed Ebola deaths
evidence: More than 1,400 cases and 438 deaths have been confirmed in the country, according to the WHO.

nary_nodes.label: No approved vaccines or treatments
evidence: There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo virus species of the disease, which is highly infectious.

nary_nodes.label: Bundibugyo virus is highly infectious
evidence: There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo virus species of the disease, which is highly infectious.

nary_nodes.label: Therapeutics could save lives
evidence: Speaking to reporters from the WHO headquarters in Geneva on Thursday, Tedros said: "Even without approved therapeutics, people are recovering from this disease, but of course, we could save many more lives with safe and effective therapeutics in our toolkit."

nary_nodes.label: Launch is significant step forward
evidence: DR Congo's Health Minister Dr Samuel Roger Kamba said the launch "represents a significant step forward, offering renewed hope to patients, their families, and affected communities".

nary_nodes.label: Ebola outbreak began
evidence: The current outbreak of Ebola in DR Congo began in May, though transmission had been going undetected for some time.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event marking the beginning of a disease outbreak.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No existing candidate accurately represents the beginning of an outbreak, so a new event type is minted.

nary_nodes.label: Public health emergency declared
evidence: The situation has been declared a public health emergency by the WHO

nary_nodes.label: Confirmed Ebola cases in DR Congo
evidence: the WHO, which says there have been 1,460 confirmed cases in DR Congo, with 150 suspected cases and 452 deaths, as of 1July.

nary_nodes.label: Suspected Ebola cases in DR Congo
evidence: the WHO, which says there have been 1,460 confirmed cases in DR Congo, with 150 suspected cases and 452 deaths, as of 1July.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola deaths in DR Congo
evidence: the WHO, which says there have been 1,460 confirmed cases in DR Congo, with 150 suspected cases and 452 deaths, as of 1July.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola recoveries in DR Congo
evidence: According to the WHO, 213 people have recovered.

nary_nodes.label: Confirmed Ebola cases in Uganda
evidence: There have also been 20 confirmed cases in Uganda, leading to two deaths, and one confirmed case in France, as of 1 July.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola deaths in Uganda
evidence: There have also been 20 confirmed cases in Uganda, leading to two deaths, and one confirmed case in France, as of 1 July.

nary_nodes.label: Confirmed Ebola case in France
evidence: There have also been 20 confirmed cases in Uganda, leading to two deaths, and one confirmed case in France, as of 1 July.

nary_nodes.label: Outbreak restricted to three provinces
evidence: Congolese health authorities have said the outbreak is currently restricted to three eastern provinces - South Kivu, North Kivu and Ituri.

nary_nodes.label: Pregnant woman tested positive for Ebola
evidence: However, the Reuters and AFP news agencies report that the body of a pregnant woman tested positive for Ebola in the neighbouring Tshopo province.

nary_nodes.label: Woman died in Ituri
evidence: The woman reportedly died in Ituri, before her body was transported by motorbike to Tshopo's main city, Kisangani, which has a population of about 1.5 million people.

nary_nodes.label: Individual fled isolation and tested positive
evidence: Additionally, an individual suspected of having Ebola reportedly fled from an isolation unit in Ituri and later tested positive in the nearby Haut-Uele province.

nary_nodes.label: Contact-tracing efforts launched
evidence: Authorities are said to have launched contact-tracing efforts across Tshopo and Haut-Uele.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event marking the initiation of contact-tracing efforts for a disease.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No existing candidate accurately represents the launch of contact tracing, so a new event type is minted.

nary_nodes.label: Public gatherings banned
evidence: Earlier this week, public gatherings were banned in both these provinces, along with neighbouring Bas-Uele and the capital, Kinshsasa, in order to prevent the spread of Ebola.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event where public gatherings are prohibited by an authority.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No existing candidate accurately represents a ban on public gatherings, so a new event type is minted.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola patients contagious after symptoms
evidence: People with Ebola usually only become contagious after developing symptoms, and it takes two to 21 days for symptoms to appear.

nary_nodes.label: Symptoms appear suddenly
evidence: They come on suddenly and start like flu or malaria with fever, headache and tiredness.

nary_nodes.label: Diagnosis improved
evidence: DR Congo's health ministry said it has improved diagnosis across the affected region.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola testing laboratories increased
evidence: Previously, four laboratories were testing for Ebola, but that number has now increased to 10 .

nary_nodes.label: Outbreak potential to be largest ever
evidence: According to both Africa CDC and US public health authorities, the current outbreak has the potential to be one of the largest ever, because it was spreading for weeks before it was confirmed to be Ebola.

nary_nodes.label: Conflict makes tackling outbreak difficult
evidence: International organisations also warn that conflict in eastern DR Congo is making it more difficult to tackle the outbreak.

nary_nodes.label: M23 controls parts of Kivu
evidence: The M23 rebel group is in control of large parts of both North and South Kivu.

nary_nodes.label: Vaccines needed for each Ebola species
evidence: Vaccines must be developed for each individual species of Ebola, of which there are six, but only three are known to cause outbreaks.

nary_nodes.label: People returned to Morocco
evidence: About 70,000 of the 72,000 people who came to Ceuta illegally last week have been returned to Morocco, Spain says.

nary_nodes.label: President absent for two months
evidence: Cameroon's president has been absent for two months while his team denies rumours about his health.

nary_nodes.label: Rocks and earth crashed onto prayers
evidence: It sent rocks and earth crashing on to those praying at an overnight service, the authorities say.

nary_nodes.label: Tens of thousands abandoned lives
evidence: Nigerian Richard Itoro is one of tens of thousands who have abandoned their lives in South Africa.

nary_nodes.label: Highway enters disputed territory
evidence: The highway enters Western Sahara, a disputed territory that Morocco claims sovereignty over.
